convoLines.text: "Every laugh out there feels wrong today. Then I feel wrong for thinking it."
A long exhale. "I'll get there. Just needed a minute where I didn't have to be fine."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"I wasn't a surgeon. I was an ESL teacher. Someone I love needed the lie more than I needed the truth."
"Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing."
"Deirdre owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"I should get back to it."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Never mind the pantry run — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. My wound needs a second pair of hands. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Get to their side of the Haven door and stand next to them — then you can help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"I dreamed Deirdre was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I hate to ask this, but I can't shake it. I'm feverish, a cut gone hot and angry. I need help. Please."
"It's not just the cut anymore, it's in the blood, I can feel it climbing. I need someone who knows wounds."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"Oh." A long pause. "I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to be left alone. The truth felt small. The lie felt like someone worth keeping around." Ananya won't meet your eyes.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"...Okay. I'll figure it out." They won't ask twice. That much is clear.
"Still on that sickness help."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Ananya rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Okay. I'll manage on my own."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"
"Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."
"These hands? Mechanic hands. Clipboards, mostly. Now they hold wire and wood, and they learn fast. Hands are honest that way."
"Funny thing — Still on what you did with your hands."
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"Deirdre is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Sleep's gone strange. I check the treeline every hour at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"The fire feels smaller without Deirdre. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"And... scene. Good talk."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Never mind the pantry run — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. I can't reach this properly. Will you help me clean it?"
"Every day it's angrier. I need it cleaned before it turns — I can't work a wound like this. Wrap it tight when you're done."
Stand beside them first — same side of the Haven door — then help.
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"Brian is gone, Ananya is gone, and Marcus is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Let me sit with all that. We'll pick it up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Hah. I keep expecting to see them by the fire. Then I remember."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Hinemoa has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. "Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything."
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "We lost Brian, Ananya and Marcus. I do the headcount without thinking. Then I think."
Their voice loosens. The guardedness thins.
"Nobody says Marcus's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Hinemoa grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Hinemoa is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening. Doesn't matter now."
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure. I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk?" David keeps their voice low. "The stores. Have you looked at the stores? We're running thin."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
It's quiet at the ridge. David doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"About this wound — I still haven't found anyone. Any chance?"
"I still need help with this wound."
You spend time tending them. This was care, not a promise of a cure.
"Still on that foraging help."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "You saw it too, right? Bring Us Something Interesting. Tell me I didn't imagine the lights."
"I should go. Before I overthink this conversation too."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I trust you? I mean really."
"Mm. That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast."
"I'll tell you what I tell everyone: watch what I do when nobody's watching. That's the whole of me. The rest is just talking."
"What's this about? Still on whether they can trust you."
"All right. Thank you for asking."
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "They took me. Bring Us Something Interesting — up there, on the screens, in front of everyone. I'm still turning it over."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Hinemoa is already 👁️ Scout — that promise is theirs.
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
You show them Stinging Nettle — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Alright. Catch you later."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

codexDeeds.text: You brought down Big-Eyes.

codexDeeds.name: Esteban
codexDeeds.text: Esteban, Phumzile brought down Big-Eyes. Together.

deeds.text: Hinemoa took the Scout role in The Company.
The Company was named — Hinemoa, David. A team, on purpose.
Hinemoa showed Asif the Ghost Pipe — leaf, stem, smell, the beginner's tour.

lastSay: d65: You camp wild tonight — no hall meal, but the pantry still reaches you through System requisition. Eat from your pack tonight.
d65: ⚠ Haven's pantry is empty. Day 5 of hunger.
d65: Haven couldn't hold. On the fifth hungry day, people started walking — in different directions. The scattering, again.
d65: 🪤 TRAP: Your Snare 2 tiles north-west caught a Gray Squirrel! About 350 kcal on the bone — clean it quickly (knife). It rots fast.
d65: The Snare broke. You'll need another.
